title: First-party-silicon agentic AI PC ships from a rival platform by H1 2027
body: Nvidia's Computex move - its first consumer PC processors in over a decade, the Arm-based N1/N1X with integrated RTX/CUDA cores, launched jointly with Microsoft as an "agentic-AI PC" that runs an assistant locally and ships this fall from Surface, Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo and MSI - does more than add one new CPU vendor. It defines a product class: a laptop where the chip maker also owns the AI stack underneath it, so a local on-device agentic assistant becomes the default experience rather than an add-on, and the device, the silicon, and the bundled agent ship as one vertically integrated tier. That AMD, Intel and Qualcomm shares fell on the news shows the market reading this as a structural threat to the merchant-silicon model of selling a CPU into someone else's box, and the same Gemma-4-on-8GB and QAT trend in this week's cycle confirms that a capable multimodal model now fits the on-device envelope these machines are built to fill. The forward consequence is that the agentic AI PC - first-party silicon plus a bundled local assistant as the default tier - hardens into the category every platform owner feels it must match, not a single Nvidia SKU. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one other major platform owner - the strongest candidates being Apple (an M-series Mac whose default Siri/Foundation-Models assistant runs fully on-device), Google with Qualcomm or MediaTek on a first-party-silicon Windows/ChromeOS-on-Arm laptop, or AMD/Intel co-launching with an OEM and Microsoft - announces a shipping or beta laptop that pairs its own first-party silicon with a bundled local agentic assistant marketed as the default tier, explicitly positioned against Nvidia's N1/N1X agentic-PC framing. A bare NPU spec bump or a cloud-routed assistant does not count; the marker is a vendor matching the full first-party-silicon-plus-default-local-agent shape.

reasoning.because: Nvidia + Microsoft launched the Arm N1/N1X as a co-designed agentic-AI PC with local on-device AI
reasoning.given: owning device base + first-party silicon + a bundled local agent now beats buying merchant CPUs
reasoning.so_that: a rival platform owner ships its own first-party-silicon laptop with a bundled local agentic assistant by default
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027, one named rival ships a first-party-silicon agentic AI-PC SKU
reasoning.plain_language: After Nvidia and Microsoft made an AI laptop with its own chip and built-in helper, a rival will build a matching one.

summary: Nvidia and Microsoft co-launched the Arm N1/N1X as an agentic AI PC pairing first-party silicon with a bundled local assistant, sending rival chip makers lower. By H1 2027 expect one rival - Apple, Google/Qualcomm, or AMD with an OEM - to ship a first-party-silicon laptop with a default local agent.
